scores.evidence: There are no images or diagrams, so nothing is decorative or broken. Comparisons use definitions tables (s1-defs, s4-defs), which read cleanly at 390 px (pages/mobile-jp-03.png, mobile-jp-12/13.png). The code blocks s2-code and p1-model keep every source line whole on mobile, with highlighted lines (pages/mobile-jp-05/06.png, mobile-jp-20.png). Nothing is clipped, overflowX is false and brokenImages is 0.

textOnlyScreens is empty on desktop-jp and mobile-jp. Every screen has a heading, table, code block, steps or a check, and paragraphs stay short. Desktop charsPerLine has a median of 37, inside the 30–40 target (max 51). Inline checks appear in every section (s1-check to s4-check), and the long practice runs are broken up by steps and checklists (pages/mobile-jp-16–23.png).

The lesson is Japanese only, and every screen is in natural Japanese with English terms in parentheses on first use (ワークツリー（worktree）, 無人実行（unattended run）). There is no untranslated UI. The link text in s3-mode names its target (公式ドキュメント（非対話的実行）). Inline code chips such as --permission-mode dontAsk and Bash(npm test *) stay whole and readable in the check-quiz options at 390 px (pages/mobile-jp-25/26.png).

niceToHave: s1-table: the three-way choice (subagent / worktree / background) is a bullet list under a two-row definitions table (pages/mobile-jp-03/04.png). A single comparison table (method × what returns × where it edits × when to use) would make the choice easier to scan.

check-quiz q3 (pages/mobile-jp-25.png): the question stem mixes six inline code chips across four lines, so it reads densely at 390 px. Consider moving the 'Bash(…) は --allowedTools の値…' explanation into a short sentence before the options, or into a smaller note.
reader: on mobile the flashcard hint says 'クリックまたはスペースキーでめくる' (pages/mobile-jp-29.png). A touch-appropriate hint (タップでめくる) would fit better.
reader: the '前のレッスン' link at the bottom of mobile runs to the right edge of the viewport (pages/mobile-jp-31.png). Consider wrapping it or adding right padding.
reader: the mobile full-length PNG is truncated at 16000px, and failed /api/ requests (14) were ignored as environment noise. The per-screen PNGs were used instead.
summary: Checked all 31 mobile-jp and 21 desktop-jp screens. Nothing fails: no overflow, no console or mermaid errors, no unknown blocks, no broken images, no text-only screens, and no personal data on any screen. Code blocks, tables and inline code chips read cleanly at 390 px. The only suggestions are optional: a single comparison table for the three parallel methods, and a lighter stem for check question 3.
